newsitem.title: HONG KONG: April start for new UPS Asian flights.
newsitem.headline: April start for new UPS Asian flights.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America plans to launch daily freighter flights from its new Asian hub in Taiwan to Manila and Bangkok in April, the company's Asia Pacific vice president Charles Adams told Reuters.
The Taipei hub is on schedule to be fully operational at the end of March then officially opened after a month of "shake-down" tests, he added.
The hub will be served by a Boeing 747 daily from Anchorage and Osaka, a daily Boeing 767 from Anchorage and Seoul and three or four Boeing 757s serving Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Manila and Bangkok.

The first new flights to the Philippines and Bangkok, initially using DC-8 aircraft before new Boeing 757 twinjets arrive, are the result of traffic rights gained late last year, Adams said in a telephone interview from his regional headquarters in Singapore.
Jakarta and Penang are possible future destinations from Taipei, he added.
The express specialist is forecasting a compound growth rate in the Asia Pacific region of around 25 per cent over the next three to five years.
The Taipei hub opening will clear the way for a potential round the world service by UPS connecting Asia with Europe and the U.S. possibly starting in 12 to 20 months time, the UPS executive said.

He added he will be meeting Philippine President Fidel Ramos in Manila on Monday when he signs a joint venture agreement for express operations with Delbros Inc, a Philippine company which has acted as a UPS agent for the past eight years.
UPS has also relocated its regional finance and billing centre just outside Metro Manila, Adams added.
